mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT lifts weekday trip chaining into shops and eateries, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when both series stop falling and print higher weekly means for at least two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -69.4 to -64.7 while TRANSIT rose from -76.4 to -73.0
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS use diverts discretionary time toward outdoor recreation and then spills back into nearby retail trips with a one- to two-week lag. When PARKS stays above zero after being negative, RETAIL_REC should improve next.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below 0 to above 0 week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -27.7 at t-2w to 5.7 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS crosses above zero and stays positive for a week but RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply suppressed, retail demand stays constrained because fewer commuters generate fewer in-person shopping trips. A further decline or stagnation in either proxy over four weeks should keep RETAIL_REC lower.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed below -73 and WORKPLACES stayed below -65 in the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay near current depressed levels but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in GROCERY_PHARM reflects substitution toward essential trips and away from discretionary shopping, which puts downward pressure on RETAIL_REC with about a one-week lag. The mechanism weakens if grocery mobility is unchanged.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -35.0 at t-2w to -29.3 at t-1w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not fall in the following week, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility keeps easing from elevated levels, households spend less time at home and more time in external venues, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks. The signal is strongest when RESIDENTIAL falls for two consecutive weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 29.3 at t-3w to 26.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its previous four-week mean within 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals denser daytime movement, and retail benefits only when both proxies rise together. The interaction should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within two weeks, not when either series improves alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved steadily from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If only one of TRANSIT or WORKPLACES improves and RETAIL_REC still rises, or if both improve together but RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An upward break in PARKS combined with lower RESIDENTIAL time indicates warmer-weather substitution into out-of-home activity, which should lift retail visitation after roughly four weeks. This works only when park use is above its recent negative range.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 0 while RESIDENTIAL falls below 27
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -27.7 to 5.7 then back to -3.6; RESIDENTIAL eased to 26.7
failure_condition: If PARKS remains above zero and RESIDENTIAL stays below 27 but RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior four-week average over the next month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in TRANSIT after a short recovery signals renewed access friction or behavior suppression, and retail follows lower with a one- to two-week lag. The effect should appear only if TRANSIT turns down from its current level.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines by at least 2 points week-on-week after t-0w
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved only modestly from -76.4 to -73.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT falls by at least 2 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not decline within the next two weeks, the hypothesis fails.
